definitions.explanation: A word adopted from another language. In Japanese linguistics, this term covers words borrowed from any foreign language, including English, Portuguese, Dutch, Chinese, and others.

examples.japanese: 「⟦パン→パン：00553_pan⟧」⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ポルトガル{語|ご}→ポルトガル語：29235_porutogarugo⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{借用語|しゃくようご}だ。
⟦{日本語|にほんご}→日本語：00614_nihongo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{英語|えいご}→英語：02274_eigo⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{借用語|しゃくようご}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{多|おお}い→多い：01127_ooi⟧。
examples.english: Japanese has many loanwords from English.

examples.japanese: {借用語|しゃくようご}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{元|もと}→元：03878_moto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{言語|げんご}→言語：02717_gengo⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{意味|いみ}→意味：01155_imi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{変|か}わる→変わる：00714_kawaru⟧こと⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Loanwords sometimes change in meaning from their original language.

notes: A linguistics term composed of ⟦{借用|しゃくよう}→借用：17718_shakuyou⟧ (borrowing) + ⟦{語|ご}→〜語：09841_go⟧ (word/language). In Japanese, loanwords are typically written in katakana and called ⟦{外来語|がいらいご}→外来語：12101_gairaigo⟧. Strictly speaking, {借用語|しゃくようご} is a broader academic term that includes ⟦{漢語|かんご}→漢語：13439_kango⟧ (Sino-Japanese words), while ⟦{外来語|がいらいご}→外来語：12101_gairaigo⟧ usually refers to non-Chinese foreign words. Related terms: ⟦{和語|わご}→和語：12074_wago⟧ (native Japanese words), ⟦{漢語|かんご}→漢語：13439_kango⟧ (Sino-Japanese words), ⟦{和製英語|わせいえいご}→和製英語：18947_waseieigo⟧ (Japanese-coined English words).
